title: Preemptive eviction tuning guidelines (WIP)
content:
TL;DR
This is a working playbook for preemptive eviction and throttling knobs to reduce OOM spike incidents caused by KV cache blowups and continuous batch queue starvation. Focus: pragmatic safety margins, observable gating, and low-risk dynamic config defaults we can roll out cluster-by-cluster.

Problem statement
- Recent incidents show an L1 pattern: sudden prefix cache growth -> batch accumulation -> host heap surge -> hard OOMs or degraded tail latency due to microbatch starvation. Root causes have varied (stale index bug, prefetch amplification, and occasional large single-tenant queries).
- We need a low-friction set of default eviction and backpressure settings that are conservative but prevent common spirals, plus an ops checklist to tune safely per cluster.

Goals
- Prevent >90% of recurring OOM spirals without materially increasing token latency for normal traffic.
- Provide observability hooks and safe rollback.
- Make settings overridable per-tenant and per-queue for Dedicated clusters.

Proposed knobs (ordered low risk -> higher impact)
1) Host-level soft heap watermark (runtime dynconfig): set soft_watermark_pct = 72% of allocatable host heap. When reached, emit metric host.eviction.soft_enter and begin batch backpressure.
2) Eviction aggressive window: eviction_window_ms = 2000 (default 20000). Short window causes more frequent small evictions rather than large delayed ones.
3) Max per-prefix cached entries cap: prefix_cache.max_entries_per_prefix = 8 -> prevents unbounded growth from a hot prefix.
4) Prefetch rate limiter: prefetch.tokens_per_sec per host, default 2000. Limit background prefetch concurrency to avoid amplification.
5) Batch admission circuit-breaker: backlog_threshold = 1500 requests per-host; when exceeded, reject non-urgent routing or downgrade to a smaller model variant.

Instrumentation & dashboards to add (minimal set)
- host.heap.usage_pct (prometheus gauge) with 5s resolution. Alert: sustained >75% for 60s -> pager to SRE-primary.
- prefix_cache.entries histogram and top-20 prefixes by entries (new es/grafana panel).
- batch.queue.length per-host and per-tenant with tail percentiles.
- eviction.* events (soft_enter, hard_enter, eviction_run, evicted_entries) as counters; correlate with OOM events.

Runbook (oncall flow)
1) Triage: check host.heap.usage_pct and eviction.* events. If host.heap >85% and evicted_entries spike -> run immediate mitigation.
2) Mitigation steps (fast)
   - Set cluster dynconfig: "eviction_window_ms" -> 2000 and "prefetch.tokens_per_sec" -> 800 via config push.
   - Trigger graceful shed: set backlog_threshold temporarily to 500 and enable model-fallback rule for non-critical routes.
   - If one tenant is responsible (top prefix shows >50% of entries), temporarily isolate tenant or move to dedicated host pool.
3) If OOM occurred: collect heap dump, kv-cache indexes, recent eviction logs, and batch queue traces. Tag incident with prefix ids.
4) Rollback criteria: if latency P95 increases >30% for >5min after changes, revert knob changes and instead isolate tenant; document in incident ticket.

Hypotheses to validate (experiment ideas)
- Shorter eviction_window_ms reduces peak heap but may increase eviction churn costs; measure token CPU increase vs heap reduction.
- Per-prefix caps stop many spirals: run controlled A/B on one region.
- Prefetch rate limiter prevents prefetch storms originating from model warmup loops in upstream client code.

Playbook testing plan
- Staging experiment: pick low-traffic region; roll dynconfig 10% hosts -> 50% -> 100% while running synthetic load with hot-prefix pattern. Monitor host.heap.usage_pct, eviction_run events, and p99 latency.
- Failure injection: simulate a large single prefix surge (synthetic client) and measure end-to-end behavior.

Open questions / risks
- Tenant isolation story for Dedicated customers needs product/SE alignment; we can throttle but moving tenants between pools frequently breaks SLAs.
- Eviction churn could increase disk I/O or CPU and thereby shift the failure mode. Need to bound cost impact.
- Prefetch limits require careful default for small hosts; propose host-class-based defaults.

Action items
- [ ] Create grafana panels and alerts (owner: Evan) (target: 2025-03-07)
- [ ] Implement dynconfig knobs in runtime config service (owner: Leo) (target: 2025-03-14)
- [ ] Staging experiments and A/B plan doc (owner: Aisha) (target: 2025-03-21)
- [ ] Add incident logging for evicted prefixes (owner: Maya) (target: 2025-03-10)

Notes to self
- Keep recommendations conservative; we can be more aggressive per-cluster after data.
- Link this doc from any future OOM postmortems as the canonical preemptive tuning starting point.

Appendix: quick diagnostics commands
- Top host heap: kubectl exec -n serving runtime-host-XYZ -- /usr/local/bin/runtime-metrics --dump | jq '.heap'
- Inspect eviction counters: curl http://$HOST:9090/metrics | grep eviction
- Query big prefixes: curl http://metrics-api/_search?q=prefix_count:>1000&sort=entries:desc

End.
